title: Polarized training has greater impact on key endurance variables than threshold, high intensity, or high volume training
population: Well-trained runners, cyclists, triathletes and cross-country skiers (VO2peak 62.6 +/- 7.1 mL/kg/min), 9 weeks, HR-controlled
findings: Four arms: high-volume (HVT), threshold (THR), high-intensity interval (HIIT) and polarized (POL).
POL gave the greatest VO2peak increase (+6.8 mL/kg/min, 11.7%, P<0.001), time to exhaustion on the ramp test +17.4% (P<0.001) and peak velocity/power +5.1% (P<0.01).

Velocity/power at 4 mmol/L increased after POL (+8.1%, P<0.01) and HIIT (+5.6%, P<0.05); no group differences in work economy; apart from slight economy gains in THR, HVT and THR produced no further changes.
limitations: Mixed sports (runners a minority), 9 weeks, small groups, no race-performance outcome. Effect sizes are far larger than later pooled estimates and were not replicated.
implications: A short (about 9-week) polarized block (about 80% low, about 20% high, minimal zone 2) is a defensible option for well-trained athletes aiming at VO2max.
Do not use the effect size as a planning assumption; later pooled evidence (Oliveira 2024, Rosenblat 2025) is much smaller.
